# Scotland Tamils Raise (STR)

## About the Organization
Scotland Tamils Raise (STR) is an Unincorporated Organisation based in Scotland, United Kingdom. It operates as a non-profit, non-political, voluntary, and charitable community organization connecting Tamil families, asylum seekers, refugees, students, and professionals residing across Edinburgh, Glasgow, Aberdeen, Dundee, Stirling, and Inverness.

## Core Purpose & Nature
- Core Purpose: To create a united, supportive, and progressive community that empowers Tamil people in Scotland while welcoming individuals from all cultures, languages, and backgrounds.
- Equality & Inclusion: Operates without discrimination based on caste, religion, gender, nationality, region, or political affiliation.
- Legal Status: Non-profit, non-political, voluntary, and charitable unincorporated organisation.

## 5 Constitutional Pillars of Activity
1. Education: Tamil language classes, tutoring, Thirukkural recitations, and literature workshops.
2. Youth & Sports Development: Sports coaching, tournaments, youth leadership summits, and career mentorship.
3. Culture & Heritage: Grand Tamil Pongal Vizha, Chithirai Tamil New Year Gala, arts showcases, Bharatanatyam, and Parai Attam folk recitals.
4. Community Welfare: Guidance, advocacy, and integration support for Tamil asylum seekers, refugees, and university students in Scotland.
5. Social & Charitable Work: Local volunteering, fundraising, food bank support, and Highland charity initiatives.

## Governance & Leadership
- Structure: Governed by an elected Board of Trustees (4 to 8 members serving 3-year terms) and Office Bearers.
- Office Bearers: Chairperson, Vice Chairperson, Secretary, and Treasurer.
- Additional Officers: Youth Coordinator, Cultural Coordinator, Sports & Wellbeing Coordinator, Community Engagement Officer, Media & Communications Officer.

## Membership Eligibility
- Eligibility: Open to individuals aged 16+ who support the aims of STR and reside in Scotland.
- Rights: Members hold voting rights at the Annual General Meeting (AGM), elect Trustees, and participate in official activities.

## Membership Tiers
- Individual Membership (£25/year) - For individuals 16+ resident in Scotland
- Family Membership (£45/year) - Covers 2 adults & children under 18 with 2 AGM votes
- Student & Youth Membership (£10/year) - For university students seeking community & mentorship
- Lifetime Patron Membership (£250 one-off) - Long-term support for Tamil heritage in Scotland
